This agreement primarily displays only the lower-division courses required in the major, and a few featured upper-division courses. Although completion of the coursework below is not necessarily mandatory prior to admission, students are strongly advised to complete as much lower division course preparation as possible prior to transfer. This agreement does not contain most upper-division (junior-senior) major requirements, course pre-requisites, general education or all-university coursework necessary for completion of this degree. ","groupId":"a7b16845-6887-ef11-8474-000d3a37e3b6","position":1,"area":"General"},{"type":"GeneralTitle","content":"General Information","groupId":"09b16845-6887-ef11-8474-000d3a37e3b6","position":2,"area":"General"},{"type":"GeneralText","content":"

Child and Family Science offers a unique set of programs that include Child Development and Family Science programs that reflect our interdisciplinary foundation from home economics. Through rigorous coursework, experiential and service learning, internships, research, and practica, students connect classroom experiences with the day-to-day world of work. Research activities and involvement in community settings give students opportunities to practice and refine skills under the mentorship of faculty and field professionals.


Advising Notes

Students majoring in Child and Family Science are required to earn a grade of C or better in all major courses.

A grade of CR/NC counts in the major only if it is the sole method of grading specified for a particular course.


Approved transfer courses include the following early childhood education/child development classes that are often used to meet requirements for the State of California Child Development Permit:

  • ECE/CHDEV 1 (Principles and Practices), ECE/CHDEV 3 (Curriculum),
  • ECE4/CHDEV 30 (Child, Family, & Community),
  • ECE 5/CHDEV 20 (Observation & Assessment),
  • ECE 10/CHDEV 37A (Practicum), ECE 40A (Administration I),
  • ECE 40B (Administration II),
  • ECE 45 (Adult Supervision),
  • or their equivalents.


Students who wish to pursue the Family Life Education Certification must complete: CFS 31, CFS 32, CFS 38, CFS 100, CFS 120, CFS 131, CFS 135, CFS 150, CFS 179, CFS 193I (with 3 units of lab for 120 hours of internship hours). More information can be found at https://www.ncfr.org/cflecertification.


In addition to the major program requirements, every student must also complete the University’s baccalaureate degree requirements such as:

  • American Government and Institutions (PLSI 2)
  • General Education Requirements (43 units)
  • Additional University Graduation Requirements (9 units)
  • Upper-Division Writing Requirement
  • General Education, Additional University Graduation Requirements, and Upper-division Writing courses can be double counted with major/additional requirements. These courses include CFS 31 (GE Area 4B), CFS 38 or CFS 39 (AUGR L/S), CFS 134 (AUGR M/I), and CFS 127W or CFS 130W, . See advisor for details.
  • Sufficient Elective Units to Meet Required Total Units (varies); it is recommended that units in this area be utilized to complete a second major or minor.

A full description of the University’s graduation requirements can be found in the Baccalaureate Degree Requirements.

Additional University Graduation Requirements


The Additional University Graduation Requirements are designed to complement the GE requirements. It is the policy of Fresno State, that all students will cultivate and refine their affective, cognitive, and physical faculties through studying great works of the human imagination; be equipped for lifelong understanding and development of themselves as integrated physiological, social, and psychological beings; and be prepared to understand and live in a multicultural and international world through their undergraduate education.

This will be accomplished through a total of 9 units from the following areas, each requiring 3 units:

  1. Arts/Humanities (A/H) - All students are required to take an Arts/Humanities course to graduate at the bachelor’s degree level. 
  2. Lifelong-Understanding and Self-Development (L/S) - All students are required to take a lifelong understanding and self-development course to for graduate at the bachelor’s degree level. 
  3. Multicultural/International (M/I) - All Students are required to take a Multicultural / International course at Fresno State to graduate at the bachelor’s degree level.
